documents.unit: THEE Pathway (General Education) common syllabus links
documents.title: Common Syllabus Links for Students: AI Policy
documents.summary: A short university AI statement in the common syllabus text: AI is allowed for listed tasks only with instructor approval, fully AI-created graded work is barred and may earn a zero, and AI use must be cited. It also bars entering confidential data into AI, and lets faculty add their own criteria.
documents.stance_why: The text says 'AI use is permissible when used for specific tasks as noted and approved by the course instructor' and that 'individual faculty, departments, and/or colleges may have additional criteria', so the decision is handed to instructors within common limits (no fully AI-made graded work, citation required); it sets no tiers, hence delegates.

units.why: The opening claim that AI 'can be a useful tool that can accelerate learning' is a rationale for permitting AI, so it is informs/general; P44 fits better than P41 because it frames AI as a learning benefit, not a shortcut.
units.anchor: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) can be a useful tool that can accelerate learning.

units.why: The policy says it 'may adjust based on this evolution at the course instructor's discretion', a statement that the policy is provisional; P54 fits (revisited/updated), though the discretion is instructor-held.
units.anchor: this policy may adjust based on this evolution at the course instructor’s discretion
units.policy: This policy may adjust as AI evolves, at the course instructor's discretion.

units.why: Faculty, departments and colleges may add syllabus criteria 'which does not conflict with this policy'; this layers local rules under the university text, so it is who-decides (P04) rather than a syllabus mandate (P09).
units.anchor: individual faculty, departments, and/or colleges may have additional criteria in their syllabus for using AI
units.policy: Individual faculty, departments, and/or colleges may have additional criteria in their syllabus for using AI that does not conflict with this policy.

units.why: States the goal that AI should 'supplement student learning, not to replace human creativity, ingenuity, or critical thinking'; a principle, and it keeps the student as thinker, so P32 rather than P56 or P41.
units.anchor: to supplement student learning, not to replace human creativity, ingenuity, or critical thinking

units.why: 'AI use is permissible when used for specific tasks as noted and approved by the course instructor' sets a permit-with-instructor-approval default; the instructor decides, so P04 over P02 since permission is conditional on approval.
units.anchor: AI use is permissible when used for specific tasks as noted and approved

units.why: Students may use AI 'to help brainstorm assignments, presentations, design ideation' with instructor approval; brainstorming matches P15.
units.anchor: to help brainstorm assignments, presentations, design ideation, etc.
units.policy: With instructor approval, students may use AI platforms to help brainstorm assignments, presentations, design ideation, etc.

units.why: 'to create a plan, outline and generate examples for assignments' is a permitted use of AI for planning; it is closest to P15 (exploring approaches) since it is not a tutor or debug use, though outlines are prose planning.
units.anchor: to create a plan, outline and generate examples for assignments;
units.policy: With instructor approval, students may use AI platforms to create a plan, outline and generate examples for assignments.

units.why: 'to summarize or synthesize sources to enhance understanding' is AI used as a study aid for understanding material, so P14 (summaries) fits better than P12.
units.anchor: to summarize or synthesize sources to enhance understanding;
units.policy: With instructor approval, students may use AI platforms to summarize or synthesize sources to enhance understanding.

units.why: 'to learn prompt engineering' is permitted; learning to use AI effectively is a skill-building aim, so P44.
units.anchor: to learn prompt engineering; crafting precise inputs (prompts) to guide AI models
units.policy: With instructor approval, students may use AI platforms to learn prompt engineering, crafting precise inputs (prompts) to guide AI models.

units.why: 'to assist in finding, analyzing, and researching sources' is a permitted research-assistance use; no type fits research help exactly, but the closest is P12 (understanding/search-engine-like use).
units.anchor: to assist in finding, analyzing, and researching sources;
units.policy: With instructor approval, students may use AI platforms to assist in finding, analyzing, and researching sources.

units.why: 'to help understand different perspectives or viewpoints' is AI used to understand ideas, i.e. a tutor-like use, P12.
units.anchor: to help understand different perspectives or viewpoints; and
units.policy: With instructor approval, students may use AI platforms to help understand different perspectives or viewpoints.

units.why: 'to enhance, improve, edit or revise their own original work' permits AI editing of prose and creative work, so P18 (prose handled separately from code).
units.anchor: to enhance, improve, edit or revise their own original work
units.frag_start: to enhance, improve, edit or revise
units.policy: With instructor approval, students may use AI platforms to enhance, improve, edit or revise their own original work (artistic, musical, written, etc.).

units.why: Warns that AI 'may also be flawed'; students are told AI outputs can be wrong, which is P31.
units.anchor: outputs that may be helpful but may also be flawed
units.frag_start: These options are with the understanding

units.why: 'no final assignment, presentation, paper, or other graded work can be fully created by AI' bans having AI produce the submitted work, P19 (unless AI is the assignment).
units.anchor: no final assignment, presentation, paper, or other graded work can be fully created by AI
units.frag_end: using AI to that end is the assignment.
units.policy: No final assignment, presentation, paper, or other graded work can be fully created by AI, unless using AI to that end is the assignment.

units.why: 'any assignments or coursework for a grade that is fully created by AI will receive a zero' states a concrete penalty, at instructor discretion; P37.
units.anchor: coursework for a grade that is fully created by AI will receive a zero
units.frag_start: At the instructor’s discretion, any assignments
units.policy: At the instructor's discretion, any graded assignment or coursework fully created by AI receives a zero for that specific assignment.

units.why: 'The unauthorized use of AI is a form of academic dishonesty' classifies misuse as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: The unauthorized use of AI is a form of academic dishonesty.

units.why: 'the submitted work must cite such usage properly' requires citation of AI use in graded work, P24 (format named but not tool/prompt details, so not P25).
units.anchor: the submitted work must cite such usage properly in accordance with current citation formats
units.frag_start: If AI is utilized for any graded work,
units.policy: If AI is utilized for any graded work, the submitted work must cite such usage properly in accordance with current citation formats (MLA, APA, Chicago, etc.).

units.why: 'The use of AI without proper citation is also a form of academic dishonesty' makes nondisclosure itself the violation, P28.
units.anchor: The use of AI without proper citation is also a form of academic dishonesty.

units.why: Links to APA, MLA and Chicago AI citation guidance as 'Guidance and examples of AI citations'; supports students in how to cite, P24 (no tool/prompt requirements stated).
units.anchor: Guidance and examples of AI citations from the main three style manuals are below.

units.why: 'prohibited from inputting any personal, sensitive, or otherwise confidential information' into any AI program, citing FERPA, HIPAA and ADA, is a data-protection ban for the whole community, P50.
units.anchor: prohibited from inputting any personal, sensitive, or otherwise confidential information
units.frag_start: Members of the JSU community are
units.policy: Members of the JSU community are prohibited from inputting any personal, sensitive, or otherwise confidential information protected under FERPA, HIPAA and the ADA into any AI program.

notes: Only the AI Policy section was coded; the Academic Honesty text in the same page does not mention AI. Page text carries no assignment-level icons.
